examples.en: Every night a stray cat rummages through the trash can.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 도둑고양이한테 사료를 챙겨 주는 분이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone in our neighborhood who feeds the stray cats.

examples.ko: 도둑고양이처럼 살금살금 들어오지 말고 인사부터 하세요.
examples.en: Don't sneak in like a stray cat; say hello first.

examples.ko: 주차장에 도둑고양이 세 마리가 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Three stray cats are gathered in the parking lot.

examples.ko: 도둑고양이였던 아이를 데려와서 이제 집에서 키워요.
examples.en: I brought home a cat that used to be a stray, and now I raise it at home.

examples.ko: 저 도둑고양이는 사람을 보면 바로 도망가요.
examples.en: That stray cat runs away as soon as it sees a person.

explain: 주인 없이 길에서 사는 고양이를 말해요. 요즘은 '길고양이'라고 더 부드럽게 말하는 사람이 많고, '도둑고양이'는 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 몰래 다니는 사람을 놀리듯 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means a cat with no owner that lives on the street. Many people now say '길고양이' (street cat), which sounds softer, while '도둑고양이' has a slightly negative feel. It can also be used to tease someone who sneaks around.

examples.en: That person's voice stands out even in the choir.

examples.ko: 흰 벽에 빨간 문이 유난히 도드라져 보여요.
examples.en: The red door stands out especially against the white wall.

examples.ko: 이 사진에서는 얼굴 윤곽이 더 도드라지게 나왔어요.
examples.en: In this photo, the outline of the face came out more prominent.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에서 수학 점수가 특히 도드라졌어요.
examples.en: My math score stood out in particular on this exam.
With makeup on, your eyes really stand out.

examples.ko: 팀에서 그 친구의 장점이 점점 도드라지고 있어요.
examples.en: That friend's strengths are becoming more and more noticeable on the team.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '두드러지다'가 있어요. 주변과 달라서 눈에 띄거나 겉으로 튀어나와 보일 때 쓰고, '도드라져 보이다' 꼴로 자주 나와요. 좋은 점이든 나쁜 점이든 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: A similar word is '두드러지다'. It is used when something differs from its surroundings and catches the eye, or sticks out, and it often appears as '도드라져 보이다'. It can describe good or bad points.

examples.en: It feels like something is missing if there is no doraji namul on the holiday table.

examples.ko: 도라지나물을 볶을 때는 소금으로 먼저 주물러요.
examples.en: When you stir-fry doraji namul, you first rub the roots with salt.
Bibimbap tastes better with doraji namul in it.
The doraji namul my mother makes is slightly bitter and nutty.

examples.ko: 저기요, 도라지나물 한 접시 더 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, could I have one more plate of doraji namul?
I seasoned doraji namul and bracken namul together.

explain: 도라지 뿌리를 무치거나 볶은 반찬이에요. 도라지는 재료 이름이고 '도라지나물'은 완성된 반찬이라서 식당 메뉴나 밥상 이야기에 나와요. 비빔밥에 들어가는 나물로도 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is a side dish made by seasoning or stir-frying bellflower roots. '도라지' is the ingredient, while '도라지나물' is the finished dish, so it shows up on menus and in talk about meals. It is also a common topping in bibimbap.

en: in affectionate whispers; with affectionate murmuring

examples.en: The family gathers and chats in warm, quiet voices.
I can hear soft, friendly voices from the kitchen.

examples.ko: 친구와 도란도란 얘기하다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: Chatting cozily with my friend, the time flew by.
I listened to old stories next to my grandmother in a cozy, quiet way.

examples.ko: 아이들이 이불 속에서 도란도란 속삭이고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are whispering cozily under the blanket.
Shall we talk quietly as we walk?

explain: '소곤소곤'은 작은 목소리에 초점이 있지만, '도란도란'은 정답고 화목한 분위기까지 담겨 있어요. 보통 '이야기하다, 말하다, 속삭이다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 싸우거나 긴장된 대화에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: '소곤소곤' focuses on a small voice, but '도란도란' also carries a warm, friendly mood. It usually goes with verbs like '이야기하다', '말하다' and '속삭이다'. It doesn't suit an argument or a tense conversation.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 도로망이 잘 갖춰져 있어요.
examples.en: This city has a well-developed road network.

examples.ko: 새 도로망 덕분에 서울까지 한 시간이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new road network, the trip to Seoul is an hour shorter.

examples.ko: 지방에도 고속도로 도로망을 더 늘려야 해요.
examples.en: We need to expand the highway network in the provinces too.
Island villages lack roads, so getting around is inconvenient.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 전국 도로망이 거의 막혔어요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy snow, the nationwide road network was almost blocked.
The road network is complicated, but I have a navigation app, so it's fine.

explain: '도로'는 길 하나하나이고, '도로망'은 그물처럼 이어진 길 전체를 말할 때 써요. 같은 '-망'이 붙은 '철도망, 통신망'도 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 뉴스나 도시 계획 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '도로' is an individual road, while '도로망' refers to the whole web of connected roads. It helps to learn other '-망' words like '철도망' and '통신망'. It often appears in the news and in talk about city planning.

examples.en: Cherry blossoms are in full bloom along the road.
You must not park on the side of the road.
Shops by the roadside are very noisy.
I met an old woman selling fruit by the roadside.
Our house is right by the road, so there is a lot of dust.

examples.ko: 도로변을 따라 가로수가 쭉 늘어서 있어요.
examples.en: Street trees line up all along the side of the road.

explain: '길가'가 일상적인 말이고, '도로변'은 차가 다니는 큰길 옆이라는 느낌이 강해요. 안내문, 간판, 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '길옆'도 있어요.
explain_en: '길가' is the everyday word, while '도로변' strongly suggests the side of a large road for vehicles. You see it on notices, signs and in the news. '길옆' is another similar word.

examples.en: This wholesaler only sells fruit by the box.

examples.ko: 시장에 도매상이 모여 있는 골목이 있어요.
examples.en: The market has an alley where wholesalers are gathered.
Buying from a wholesaler is much cheaper than at a store.
My father runs a stationery wholesale business.
I get goods from a wholesaler and pass them on to retail shops.

examples.ko: 새벽에 도매상까지 가서 꽃을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I went all the way to the wholesaler at dawn and bought flowers.

explain: 물건을 많이 사서 가게에 넘기는 가게나 사람이에요. 반대말은 '소매상'이고, 가격 이야기에서는 '도매가'처럼 쓰여요. 보통 손님 한 명에게 팔지 않고 가게 주인에게 팔아요.
explain_en: It is a shop or person that buys goods in bulk and sells them on to other stores. The opposite is '소매상' (retailer), and in price talk you hear '도매가' (wholesale price). It usually sells to shop owners, not to individual customers.

examples.en: I chose a light-colored wallpaper.

examples.ko: 이 도배지는 물걸레로 닦을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can wipe this wallpaper with a damp cloth.

examples.ko: 벽에 곰팡이가 생겨서 도배지를 새로 붙여야 해요.
examples.en: Mold grew on the wall, so we have to put up new wallpaper.

examples.ko: 도배지 샘플을 몇 개 받아 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a few wallpaper samples.

examples.ko: 낡은 도배지가 뜯어져서 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The old wallpaper is peeling off and looks bad.
The wallpaper pattern is too flashy, so I'm hesitating.

explain: '벽지'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 집을 고치거나 이사할 때 '도배하다, 도배지를 고르다'처럼 도배 작업과 함께 자주 나와요. 도배 작업은 보통 전문 업체에 맡겨요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '벽지' (wallpaper). When people renovate or move, it appears together with the job itself, as in '도배하다' and '도배지를 고르다'. The work is usually left to a professional company.

examples.en: I went to class wearing my taekwondo uniform.
The belt color on my uniform is blue now.

examples.ko: 아들이 도복 입은 모습이 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: My son looks really cool in his uniform.
I washed the uniform and hung it out on the balcony.
A judo uniform is thick, so it's hot in summer.

examples.ko: 도복 가방을 안 가져와서 다시 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I forgot my uniform bag, so I went back home.

explain: 태권도, 유도, 검도처럼 무술을 할 때 입는 옷이에요. '태권도복, 유도복'처럼 종목 이름을 앞에 붙여 말하기도 해요. 태권도와 유도 도복은 허리에 띠를 매고, 띠 색깔로 실력 단계를 나타내요.
explain_en: It is the clothing worn for martial arts such as taekwondo, judo and kendo. People also put the sport in front, as in '태권도복' and '유도복'. Taekwondo and judo uniforms are worn with a belt at the waist, and the belt color shows the level.

examples.en: Our apartment building has city gas supplied.

examples.ko: 도시가스 요금이 이번 달에 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The gas bill came out high this month.
The gas meter reader came and checked the meter.
When you move, you should first apply for gas service.
The country house has no city gas, so it uses an oil boiler.
After switching to city gas, my heating costs went down.

explain: 배관을 통해 집으로 바로 들어오는 가스예요. 통에 담아 배달받는 가스(LPG)와는 달라요. 요금 고지서나 이사할 때 신청하는 일 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is gas that comes straight into the home through pipes, unlike bottled gas (LPG) that gets delivered in tanks. It often comes up with utility bills and when applying for service as you move.

examples.en: City people head out to nature every weekend.
Busy city people really need rest.
A city dweller's life is very different from life in the countryside.

examples.ko: 저는 도시인이라 별이 보이는 밤이 신기해요.
examples.en: I'm a city person, so a night with visible stars feels amazing.
As city dwellers increased, the countryside grew quieter.

examples.ko: 도시인처럼 입고 다니니까 시골 어르신들이 쳐다보셨어요.
examples.en: Because I dressed like a city person, the elderly villagers looked at me.

explain: 도시에 살면서 도시의 생활 방식에 익숙한 사람을 말해요. 반대되는 말은 '시골 사람'이나 '농촌 사람'이에요. 대화에서는 '서울 사람'처럼 구체적으로 말하는 일이 많고, '도시인'은 기사나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who lives in a city and is used to the city lifestyle. The opposite is '시골 사람' or '농촌 사람'. In conversation people often say something specific like '서울 사람', while '도시인' appears more in articles and writing.

examples.en: This area is urbanizing quickly.

examples.ko: 농촌이 도시화하면서 논밭이 줄고 아파트가 늘었어요.
examples.en: As the rural area urbanized, fields decreased and apartments increased.
In a village that has become urbanized, neighbors don't know each other well.
Before the island urbanized, it was a quiet fishing village.
It became urbanized and more convenient, but the air got worse.
The pace of urbanization is so fast that I'm worried.

explain: 사회 수업이나 뉴스에서 주로 쓰는 말이에요. 같은 흐름의 말로 '산업화하다, 현대화하다'가 있어요. '도시화'라는 명사로 '도시화가 진행되다'처럼도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This word is mainly used in social studies classes and the news. Words in the same family include '산업화하다' and '현대화하다'. The noun '도시화' also appears often, as in '도시화가 진행되다'.

examples.en: If there's something you don't know, click Help.

examples.ko: 선생님이 짧은 도움말을 한마디 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave me a short word of advice.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 도움말이 한국어로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This program's help section is in Korean.

examples.ko: 그분의 도움말 덕분에 문제를 쉽게 풀었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to that person's tip, I solved the problem easily.
If you need any advice, just tell me anytime.

examples.ko: 면접 준비에 도움말을 주실 분 계세요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who can give me some tips for interview prep?

explain: '조언'보다 가볍고 짧게, 도움이 되는 말을 해 줄 때 써요. 컴퓨터 프로그램의 '도움말(Help)' 메뉴도 같은 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '힌트'도 있지만 '도움말'은 문제 풀이뿐 아니라 일상 조언에도 써요.
explain_en: It is lighter and shorter than '조언' (advice) and is used when someone says something helpful. The 'Help' menu in computer programs is also called '도움말'. A similar word is '힌트' (hint), but '도움말' also covers everyday advice, not just solving problems.

examples.en: The rookie challenged the champion.
A small company threw down the gauntlet to a big corporation.
When the challenge arrived, everyone got nervous.

examples.ko: 우리 반이 옆 반에 축구 도전장을 보냈어요.
examples.en: Our class sent a soccer challenge to the next class.

examples.ko: 저는 그 도전장을 기꺼이 받아들이기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to gladly accept that challenge.

examples.ko: 도전장은 받았으니 이제 열심히 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: I've received the challenge, so now I have to prepare hard.

explain: 원래는 싸움이나 경기를 신청하는 글이지만, 지금은 비유로 많이 써요. '도전장을 내밀다, 던지다'는 도전하는 쪽에서, '도전장을 받다'는 도전을 받는 쪽에서 말해요. 뉴스나 스포츠 기사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 신인 감독이 최고 감독에게 도전장을 내밀었어요.
phrases.en: A rookie director took on the top director.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 편지가 없어도 경쟁이나 대결에 나선다는 뜻으로 써요. 주로 약한 쪽이 강한 쪽에 맞설 때 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: No actual letter is involved; it means stepping forward to compete or confront. It is often said when a weaker side takes on a stronger one.

explain_en: It originally meant a written request for a fight or match, but today it is mostly used figuratively. '도전장을 내밀다/던지다' is said by the challenger, and '도전장을 받다' by the one being challenged. You often see it in news and sports articles.

examples.en: I dip the acorn jelly in seasoned sauce and eat it.
After hiking, I ate seasoned acorn jelly.
They say acorn jelly is low in calories, so it's good for dieting.

examples.ko: 저기요, 도토리묵 한 접시랑 파전 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one plate of acorn jelly and a scallion pancake, please.
My grandmother made acorn jelly herself for us.

examples.ko: 차가운 도토리묵이 여름에 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: Cold acorn jelly revives your appetite in summer.

explain: 도토리 가루로 만든 묵이에요. 청포묵, 메밀묵처럼 재료에 따라 이름이 달라요. 묵은 '만들다'보다 '쑤다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a jelly made from acorn starch. Like 청포묵 and 메밀묵, its name changes depending on the ingredient. For making muk, people often say '쑤다' rather than '만들다'.

examples.en: For him, books were a refuge from a hard reality.
Travel shouldn't become an escape.

examples.ko: 게임이 유일한 도피처라고 말하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who says games are the only place to escape to.

examples.ko: 그는 해외로 떠날 도피처를 찾고 있었어요.
examples.en: He was looking for a place to flee abroad.
This little cafe is my refuge.
Some people choose the countryside as a place to escape to.

explain: '쉼터'나 '안식처'는 편히 쉬는 곳이라 따뜻한 느낌이에요. 반면 '도피처'는 힘든 일이나 책임을 피해 숨는 곳이라 조금 부정적일 때가 많아요. 사람의 마음이나 취미를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '쉼터' and '안식처' are places to rest and feel warm. '도피처', by contrast, is a place to hide from hardship or responsibility, so it often sounds a bit negative. It can also describe a person's mind or hobby metaphorically.

examples.ko: 아이가 주운 나뭇잎을 도화지에 붙여서 그림을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child stuck the leaves they picked up onto drawing paper and made a picture.

examples.ko: 문방구에서 도화지 두 장만 사 주세요.
examples.en: Please buy two sheets of drawing paper at the stationery store.
The drawing paper was thin, so the paint bled.
She's a child with a pure heart, like blank white paper.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 큰 도화지를 나눠 받았어요.
examples.en: In art class, we were each handed a large sheet of drawing paper.

examples.ko: 도화지 한 장에 우리 가족을 그렸어요.
examples.en: I drew my family on one sheet of drawing paper.

explain: 그림을 그리는 두껍고 하얀 종이예요. 학교 미술 시간에 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 여러 장이 묶여 있는 것은 '스케치북'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is thick white paper for drawing, a word often used in school art class. A bound pad of many sheets is called a '스케치북' (sketchbook).

examples.en: I want to nurture my child's independence.
That newspaper is trusted because of its strong independence.

examples.ko: 독립성이 강한 아이는 혼자서도 잘 놀아요.
examples.en: A child with a strong sense of independence plays well alone.
The independence of the courts is important for democracy.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 독립성을 보장받아서 자유롭게 일해요.
examples.en: This team is guaranteed independence, so it works freely.

examples.ko: 독립성과 협동심을 같이 기를 수 있는 활동이에요.
examples.en: It's an activity where you can build both independence and teamwork.

explain: 남에게 기대지 않고 스스로 하는 성질이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 신문, 법원, 기관 같은 곳에도 써요. 반대되는 말은 '의존성'이에요.
explain_en: It means the quality of acting on your own without leaning on others. It applies not only to people but also to newspapers, courts and other institutions. The opposite is '의존성' (dependence).

examples.en: My great-grandfather was someone who took part in the independence movement.

examples.ko: 독립운동가의 후손들이 기념식에 초대돼 감사패를 받았어요.
examples.en: Descendants of independence activists were invited to the ceremony and received plaques of appreciation.
The liberation of 1945 came after a long independence movement.
I learned the history of the independence movement at school.

examples.ko: 독립운동 때문에 감옥에 간 분들도 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people went to prison because of the independence movement.
The museum is exhibiting materials on the independence movement.

explain: 한국에서는 일제강점기에 나라를 되찾으려 한 활동을 가리킬 때 가장 많이 써요. 그 일을 한 사람은 '독립운동가'라고 해요. 같은 맥락에서 '광복'이나 '3·1 운동'도 함께 배워요.
explain_en: In Korea this most often refers to the activities to regain the country during the Japanese colonial period. A person who took part is called a '독립운동가'. In the same context you also learn '광복' (liberation) and the '3·1 Movement'.

examples.ko: 산에서 모르는 버섯은 독버섯일 수 있어요.
examples.en: A mushroom you don't know in the mountains could be poisonous.

examples.ko: 독버섯은 색이 화려하다고 하지만 꼭 그렇지는 않아요.
examples.en: They say poisonous mushrooms are colorful, but that isn't always true.

examples.ko: 독버섯을 잘못 먹고 병원에 간 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone ate a poisonous mushroom by mistake and went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 독버섯이랑 식용 버섯은 구별이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's hard to tell poisonous mushrooms and edible ones apart.

examples.ko: 독버섯 사진을 보면서 위험한 버섯을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about dangerous mushrooms by looking at photos of poisonous ones.
Bad rumors spread quickly, like poisonous mushrooms.

explain: 독이 있어서 먹으면 위험한 버섯이에요. 반대되는 말은 '식용 버섯'이에요. 나쁜 것이 몰래 퍼지는 모습을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a mushroom that contains poison and is dangerous to eat. The opposite is '식용 버섯' (edible mushroom). It is also used figuratively for bad things that spread quietly.

en: picture taken of one individual alone

examples.en: I took a solo photo for my passport.

examples.ko: 단체 사진 말고 독사진도 한 장 찍어 주세요.
examples.en: Besides the group photo, please take a solo picture of me too.
Solo photos feel awkward, so my expression always stiffens.

examples.ko: 여행 가서 독사진을 열 장이나 건졌어요.
examples.en: I got as many as ten solo shots on the trip.
I like this solo photo the best.

examples.ko: 졸업 앨범에 들어갈 독사진 촬영이 오늘이에요.
examples.en: Today is the solo photo shoot for the graduation album.

explain: 혼자 찍은 사진을 짧게 부르는 말이에요. 반대되는 말은 '단체 사진'이나 '커플 사진'이에요. '혼자 찍은 사진'이라고 길게 말하는 것보다 일상에서 더 편하게 써요.
explain_en: It is a short word for a photo of just one person. The opposites are '단체 사진' (group photo) or '커플 사진' (couple photo). It is more convenient in daily speech than saying the longer '혼자 찍은 사진'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a well-known bookworm.
The teacher's room is full of books because they love reading.

examples.ko: 저도 독서광이 되고 싶은데 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: I want to be a bookworm too, but I have no time.
Being a bookworm, I don't put my book down even on the subway.
I heard that author was a bookworm from a young age.
I joined an online group where bookworms gather.

explain: 책을 아주 많이 읽는 사람이에요. '책벌레'도 비슷한 말인데, 더 친근하고 가볍게 들려요. '-광'은 '영화광, 축구광'처럼 어떤 것에 푹 빠진 사람을 말해요.
explain_en: It means a person who reads a great many books. '책벌레' is similar but sounds friendlier and lighter. The suffix '-광' marks someone absorbed in something, as in '영화광' and '축구광'.

examples.ko: 독신자를 위한 소형 아파트가 인기를 끌고 있어요.
examples.en: Small apartments for single people are gaining popularity.

examples.ko: 이 기숙사는 독신자만 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only unmarried people can apply for this dormitory.
The number of single-person households is growing every year.

examples.ko: 독신자가 늘면서 혼자 먹는 식당도 많아졌어요.
examples.en: As singles increased, restaurants for eating alone also became common.
He is single, so he is free even after work.
I made new friends at a gathering for singles.

explain: '미혼'은 아직 결혼하지 않은 사람이고, '독신자'는 이혼이나 사별 뒤에 혼자 사는 사람도 포함해요. 일상 대화에서는 '싱글'이나 '혼자 사는 사람'이라고 더 자주 말하고, '독신자'는 뉴스, 서류, 통계에서 많이 보여요. 반대는 '기혼자'예요.
explain_en: '미혼' means someone who has not married yet, while '독신자' also includes people living alone after divorce or bereavement. In daily talk people more often say '싱글' or '혼자 사는 사람', and '독신자' shows up in the news, documents and statistics. The opposite is '기혼자' (married person).

en: choosing to stay single; the principle of remaining unmarried

examples.en: I choose to stay single, so I have no plans to marry.

examples.ko: 독신주의를 선택하는 사람이 점점 많아지고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are choosing to stay single.
My friend was set on staying single but got married last year.

examples.ko: 독신주의자인 이모는 혼자 여행을 자주 가세요.
examples.en: My aunt, who has chosen to stay single, often travels alone.
My parents don't understand my choice to stay single.
Choosing to stay single doesn't mean you're lonely.

explain: 결혼하지 않고 혼자 살겠다는 생각이나 태도예요. 그런 사람은 '독신주의자'라고 해요. 한국어에서는 결혼 여부에 대한 말이지, 연애나 성적인 금욕을 뜻하지 않아요.
explain_en: It means the view or attitude of choosing not to marry and to live alone, and such a person is called a '독신주의자'. It is about marriage status, not about dating or sexual abstinence.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 시장에서 독점적 지위를 갖고 있어요.
examples.en: That company holds a monopolistic position in the market.

examples.ko: 독점적 권리 때문에 다른 회사는 같은 제품을 못 팔아요.
examples.en: Because of exclusive rights, other companies can't sell the same product.

examples.ko: 한 업체가 독점적으로 물건을 공급하고 있어요.
examples.en: One company supplies the goods exclusively.
This contract grants exclusive sales rights.

examples.ko: 독점적 구조 때문에 가격이 계속 올라요.
examples.en: Because of the monopolistic structure, prices keep rising.
It's a company with exclusive broadcasting rights.

explain: '독점' 뒤에 '-적'이 붙은 말로, '독점적 지위'처럼 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요. '독점적으로', '독점적이다', '독점적인'처럼 활용해서도 써요. 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 한 곳이 혼자 다 차지한다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is '독점' plus '-적', used before a noun as in '독점적 지위'. It also appears as '독점적으로', '독점적이다' and '독점적인'. It is common in economic news and gives the feeling that one party takes everything for itself.

examples.en: We rented the whole pension and had fun as a family.

examples.ko: 독채라서 소음 걱정 없이 지낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a standalone house, so you can stay without worrying about noise.
This house is a whole-house jeonse, so it's expensive.
I booked a whole hanok house for our stay.

examples.ko: 독채를 쓰니까 마당도 마음대로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Since we use the whole house, we can use the yard freely too.

examples.ko: 원룸 말고 독채로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move into a standalone house instead of a studio.

explain: 다른 사람과 나누지 않고 건물 한 채를 통째로 쓰는 것을 말해요. 방 하나만 빌리는 경우와 비교할 때 써요. 펜션이나 한옥 숙소를 예약할 때 자주 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means using a whole building by yourself without sharing it with others. It's used in contrast with renting just one room. You often see it when booking a pension or hanok stay.

examples.en: The funding dried up, so the shop closed.

examples.ko: 그 사업가가 정치인의 돈줄이라는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that the businessman is the politician's financial backer.

examples.ko: 돈줄을 쥐고 있는 사람이 결국 결정해요.
examples.en: The person who holds the purse strings makes the final decision.
The father said he would cut off his son's money supply.

examples.ko: 돈줄이 마르면 회사는 오래 못 버텨요.
examples.en: If the funding runs dry, a company can't hold on for long.

examples.ko: 새 돈줄을 찾아야 공연을 계속할 수 있어요.
examples.en: We need to find a new source of money to keep the show going.

explain: 돈을 대 주는 사람이나 돈이 들어오는 길을 가리켜요. '돈줄이 막히다, 마르다, 끊기다'처럼 자금이 끊기는 상황에 많이 써요. 조금 속된 느낌이 있고, 비슷한 말로 '자금줄'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the person who supplies money or the channel through which money comes in. It's often used for cut-off funding, as in '돈줄이 막히다', '마르다' and '끊기다'. It has a slightly informal feel, and a similar word is '자금줄'.

examples.en: Grandfather reads the newspaper wearing reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기로 보면 곤충의 날개가 자세히 보여요.
examples.en: With a magnifying glass, you can see an insect's wings in detail.
My eyesight got worse, so I started to need reading glasses.
The researcher looked through a magnifying glass all day.

examples.ko: 작은 글씨는 돋보기 없이 못 읽어요.
examples.en: I can't read small print without reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기 앱을 켜면 스마트폰으로 글씨를 키울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you open a magnifier app, you can enlarge text on your smartphone.

explain: 작은 것을 크게 보는 렌즈도 '돋보기'이고, 나이가 들어 가까운 글씨가 안 보일 때 쓰는 안경도 '돋보기'라고 해요. 안경을 분명히 말할 때는 '돋보기안경'이라고도 해요. 스마트폰의 확대 기능도 '돋보기'라고 불러요.
explain_en: A lens that enlarges small things is a '돋보기', and so are the glasses people wear when close-up text gets hard to see with age. To make clear it's glasses, people also say '돋보기안경'. The zoom feature on smartphones is called '돋보기' too.

examples.en: My mother sews wearing her reading glasses.
I can't see the menu without reading glasses.
I don't know where I put my reading glasses.
As you get older, you come to need reading glasses.
The strength of my reading glasses doesn't suit me, so I feel dizzy.
You can get reading glasses made at an optician's.

explain: 가까이 있는 글씨를 볼 때 쓰는 안경이에요. 줄여서 '돋보기'라고 많이 말해요. 멀리 있는 것을 잘 보게 하는 안경과는 용도가 달라요.
explain_en: These are glasses used to see text up close. People often shorten the word to '돋보기'. Their purpose is different from glasses that help you see things far away.

examples.en: I sprained my ankle walking on a stony path.
The stony mountain path is slippery, so be careful.

examples.ko: 돌길 위를 달리니까 차가 많이 흔들려요.
examples.en: Driving on a stony road shakes the car a lot.

examples.ko: 시골 마을의 돌길을 따라 걸으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Walking along the stone paths of a country village makes me feel calm.
The rain made the stony path more dangerous.

examples.ko: 돌길에는 운동화를 신고 가는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On a stony path, it's better to wear sneakers.

explain: 돌이 깔려 있거나 돌이 많은 길이에요. 작은 돌이 깔린 길은 '자갈길'이라고 하고, 흙으로 된 길은 '흙길'이라고 해요. 걷기 불편하다는 느낌으로 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a path paved with stones or full of stones. A path of small stones is a '자갈길', and a dirt path is a '흙길'. It is often said with the feeling that the path is uncomfortable to walk on.

examples.en: There are many stone walls on Jeju Island.

examples.ko: 마을 가옥들은 대부분 돌담으로 둘러싸여 있어요.
examples.en: Most houses in the village are surrounded by stone walls.
A cat is walking along the top of the stone wall.
Little flowers have bloomed at the foot of the stone wall.
I can see the neighbor's yard over the stone wall.
It's a low stone wall, so it's easy to climb over.

explain: 돌을 쌓아서 만든 담이에요. 흙담이나 시멘트 담과 재료가 달라요. 제주도나 시골 마을의 옛 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a wall built by stacking stones, different in material from an earth wall or a cement wall. It often appears when describing old scenery on Jeju Island or in country villages.

en: lump of rock; chunk of stone

examples.ko: 길 한가운데 큰 돌덩이가 떨어져 있었어요.
examples.en: A big chunk of rock was lying in the middle of the road.

examples.ko: 체했는지 속에 돌덩이가 들어 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Maybe it's indigestion; it feels like there's a rock in my stomach.
It's dangerous if children throw chunks of rock.
My shoulders are knotted up like rocks.
It was hard picking out rocks from the field.

examples.ko: 돌덩이 하나가 굴러 내려와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A chunk of rock rolled down, and I was startled.

explain: 작은 '돌멩이'보다 크고 단단한 덩어리를 말하고, 아주 큰 것은 '바위'라고 해요. 몸이나 마음이 무겁고 굳었을 때 '돌덩이 같다, 돌덩이처럼 무겁다'라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means a hard lump bigger than a small '돌멩이' (pebble), and something very large is called a '바위' (boulder). When the body or mind feels heavy and stiff, people say '돌덩이 같다' or '돌덩이처럼 무겁다' metaphorically.
